planting.note: Plant rooted offshoots or tissue-cultured plantlets in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing trees widely to allow their eventual crown spread.

directions: Plant rooted offshoots or tissue-cultured plantlets in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, spacing trees widely to allow their eventual crown spread; Khalas thrives only where summers are long, intensely hot, and dry enough to properly cure the ripening fruit. One of the most widely planted and commercially valuable dates across the UAE, Saudi Arabia's Al-Ahsa oasis, and Bahrain, Khalas is prized as an all-purpose eating date, sold at both the soft amber rutab stage and the firmer, chewier dried tamr stage. Female trees need a male pollinator or hand pollination to set fruit, and new offshoots typically take five to seven years before bearing a full commercial crop.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences
FAO Regional Office for the Near East and North Africa

planting.note: Establish from offshoots or lab-propagated plantlets in spring, giving each tree deep, well-drained soil, full desert sun, and ample room to mature.

directions: Establish from offshoots or lab-propagated plantlets in spring, giving each tree deep, well-drained soil, full desert sun, and ample room to mature; like other date palms, Fardh needs a long, searingly hot, low-humidity summer to ripen and cure its crop properly. It is Oman's single most widely cultivated date variety, grown extensively across the interior plantations of the Sharqiyah region around Ibra and Al Mudhaibi, forming the backbone of the country's date export economy. The medium-sized, semi-dry fruit is harvested mostly for drying and storage rather than fresh eating, valued for reliable yields, long shelf life, and suitability for the traditional Omani practice of packing cured dates for sale and export.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences
Oman Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources
FAO Regional Office for the Near East and North Africa

planting.note: Plant offshoots in deep, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, watering generously through establishment.

directions: Plant offshoots in deep, well-drained soil in full sun in spring, watering generously through establishment since young palms need consistent moisture even though mature trees are drought-tolerant once deep roots develop. Khunaizi is grown widely across Oman's Al Batinah coastal plain, where it is valued as a soft-textured, richly sweet eating date typically harvested and consumed fresh at the rutab stage rather than fully dried. Its dark, glossy skin and tender flesh make it popular in local markets during date season, though it does not store or ship as well as firmer drying varieties. As with all date palms, separate male and female trees are needed for pollination, and new plantings take roughly five to seven years to reach full bearing.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences
Oman Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

planting.note: Grow from offshoots or tissue-cultured starts planted in spring into deep, well-drained soil under full desert sun.

directions: Grow from offshoots or tissue-cultured starts planted in spring into deep, well-drained soil under full desert sun, allowing years of hot, dry summers for the tree to mature and ripen its fruit properly. Khudri, also called Al-Khudari, is grown extensively around Medina in Saudi Arabia and is one of the most widely consumed everyday dates in the region, valued for its dark brown-to-black color and firm, chewy, mildly sweet flesh that is less cloying than premium varieties. It is eaten at both the crisp, tannic khalal stage and the fully cured tamr stage, and is also a common base for inexpensive date paste and syrup. Hand pollination of female flowers and patient multi-year establishment are standard practice, as with other commercial date cultivars.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences
FAO Regional Office for the Near East and North Africa

planting.note: Plant nursery-grown trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, watering regularly during establishment.

directions: Plant nursery-grown trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, watering regularly during establishment but letting the soil dry slightly between waterings once mature, since limes dislike waterlogged roots. This small, thin-skinned, highly aromatic lime is grown in Oman's interior mountain oases, particularly around the Jebel Akhdar terraces, and is the traditional source of loomi, the sun-dried black limes essential to Gulf, Iraqi, and Iranian cooking. Fruit destined for drying is harvested while still green or just turning yellow, boiled briefly in salted water, then sun-dried for one to two weeks until the rind turns dark brown to black and hardens completely; whole dried limes are cracked and simmered into stews, rice dishes, and fish curries for their distinctive musty-sour aroma. Trees are frost-tender and need protection below the high 20s F, but otherwise need only routine citrus care.
sources: Sultan Qaboos University College of Agricultural and Marine Sciences
FAO Regional Office for the Near East and North Africa
Oman Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

planting.note: Direct-sow after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed, planting in blocks rather than single rows for reliable wind pollination.

directions: Direct-sow seed after the soil has warmed and frost danger has passed, planting in blocks rather than single rows to ensure reliable wind pollination, and hill soil around stalk bases as they grow for better anchorage. Avati Morotï, whose Guarani name simply means 'white corn,' is a traditional Paraguayan flint maize landrace grown by small farmers for generations and dried on the stalk for use as whole hominy-style kernels, ground meal, and the base starch for chipa guasu and mazamorra. Its hard, starchy white kernels store well after drying and are valued for flavor and texture in traditional dishes rather than for fresh eating. Side-dress with compost or manure at knee height for best ear development, and let ears dry fully in the husk before harvesting for storage grain.
sources: Paraguayan Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG)
FAO Regional Office for Latin America and the Caribbean
